=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Draft (SPA and Disclosure Letter)

**Scope note:** I've reviewed the whole package, not just the items marked [OPEN]. The [STANDARD] and "cleared" labels, the "FINAL / not to be re-opened" language, and the market-practice claims are the Seller's characterisations. They don't bind Wattlebridge. Several of the clauses labelled [STANDARD] are the most material ones in the package.

## 1. Most serious issues

**(a) Buyer-knowledge clause (cl 8.3) combined with general data-room disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2).**
Together these would remove most of the claims we would need. The Seller discloses "every fact... contained or referred to" in the data room, and the Buyer is barred from claiming on anything it "had knowledge of," including anything "discoverable" from the data room. We know about every issue in the Disclosure Letter, so under this drafting we would have no claim for any of them. Known exposures alone total about AUD 4.13m (see section 4), close to the proposed AUD 4.8m cap. Both provisions should be rejected. We should insist on a pro-sandbagging clause and on specific indemnities for known matters. Disclosure should be against specific warranties and fairly disclosed, not general.

**(b) Liability cap, de minimis and basket (cl 12.1–12.2).**
- The cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) is the top of the range the Seller itself quotes, and it applies to all general warranties. That leaves no room for negotiation on the general warranties and no protection for the fundamental ones.
- A AUD 25,000 de minimis plus a AUD 250,000 basket, with recovery only of the excess, means the Buyer absorbs roughly the first AUD 250,000 of every warranty loss. Claims from related facts may be argued to be separate, which makes the threshold worse.
- Push for a first-dollar (tipping) basket, a lower de minimis, aggregation of related claims, and an exclusion of specific indemnities and fundamental warranties from both thresholds.

**(c) Fundamental and title warranties (cl 12, "administrative simplicity").**
Title and capacity warranties should not be subject to the general cap or the 18-month period. Resist this firmly. Fundamental warranties should be capped at the purchase price (or at least well above the general cap), with a limitation period of at least six years, and should sit outside the basket and de minimis.

**(d) Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applied to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5).**
Insist on carve-outs for fraud, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and wilful concealment. Fraud should not be excludable by contract, but the drafting should say so expressly.

## 2. Other drafting issues

- **Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13):** 18 months is short for a SaaS business with tax, IP and privacy exposure. Push for 24 to 36 months for general warranties, and longer for tax (tied to the ATO assessment period) and fundamental warranties. Check how the contractual limits interact with the statutory limitation period under NSW law.
- **Bluefen conditions (cl 3 / 6.3):** Treating consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's consent, with only reasonable endeavours from the Seller, is not enough. Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (AUD 3.6m), and DL 2 confirms that the final consent and the cl 11.3 conditions are not met. Make the consent a condition precedent, or provide a specific indemnity and a price adjustment or escrow.
- **Riverlark (cl 2 / 7):** The facility is about AUD 3.2m and has not been repaid. A "release following Completion" is inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free basis. The debt should be deducted from price and repaid at Completion, with a payout letter and discharge of security delivered at Completion. The funds flow should reconcile to this.
- **Ironquay IP (cl 11.1):** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment. DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on payment, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. The indemnity should cover third-party claims, redevelopment costs and lost value, and should not be limited to the fee. Payment and a confirmatory assignment should be conditions precedent.
- **Stale disclosure:** The data room cut-off is 5.00pm 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026. Require a bring-down disclosure before Completion, with a Buyer right to walk away or claim if material changes arise.

## 3. Items to verify with the Seller

| Area | Issue | Required position |
|---|---|---|
| Bonuses (DL 5) | AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses are missing from the funds flow. Payroll tax and super are not addressed. | Treat as a debt-like item deducted from price. Seller bears all on-costs. Specific indemnity. |
| Privacy incident (DL 6) | About 1,240 records of names, emails, roles and timestamps may have been sent to an unintended external address. Not yet known whether anyone accessed it or whether notification is required. | Urgent. Under the Privacy Act's Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an assessment is generally required within 30 days of awareness. Establish when the Company became aware. Require an immediate forensic review and a specific indemnity outside the cap covering regulatory, notification and third-party costs. Add a warranty of no eligible data breach. |
| Supplier renewals (DL 8) | Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each. Seller calls them ordinary course. | Obtain the contracts. Check term, termination rights and whether they are non-ordinary-course commitments. Price or indemnify any unavoidable excess. |
| Office lease (DL 7) | Notification obligation. Landlord consent for the share sale is not confirmed. | Confirm in writing whether consent or a waiver is needed. If so, make it a condition precedent. |
| Mossvale (DL 9) | Restriction on assignment. Whether a change of control triggers it is not stated. | Confirm the trigger. Obtain consent or a waiver if needed. |
| Title (DL 10, DD-012) | The Seller relies on its own share register. | Independent verification: ASIC company and share searches, PPSR search for encumbrances, original share certificates, and transfer forms. Title warranty to be fundamental. |

## 4. Known exposure (quantified)

| Item | AUD |
|---|---|
| Riverlark debt (should be deducted from price, not a warranty claim) | 3,200,000 |
| Completion bonuses (plus on-costs, not yet quantified) | 420,000 |
| Ironquay SOW3 open payment (not bank-verified) | 180,000 |
| Supplier renewals | 330,000 |
| **Total quantified** | **4,130,000** |

The Bluefen revenue risk (about AUD 3.6m of revenue) and the privacy exposure are not quantified above. Bluefen should be addressed through consent, price or escrow. The Riverlark figure should be dealt with through the debt mechanism to avoid double counting.

## 5. Recommendations

1. **Reject cl 8.3** (buyer knowledge) and **the general data-room disclosure**. Replace them with a pro-sandbagging clause and specific disclosure only.
2. **Reject the Seller's characterisation of the package as FINAL.** Negotiate the cap, basket and de minimis on their merits. Test the Seller's "market" claims with precedent data before accepting them.
3. **Raise the general cap** above 20%, and cap fundamental and tax warranties at the purchase price.
4. **Replace the basket** with a first-dollar threshold and a lower de minimis, with aggregation of related claims. Exclude specific indemnities and fundamental warranties.
5. **Keep fundamental warranties outside the general time limit**, with at least six years.
6. **Carve out fraud, specific indemnities and tax** from the limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions.
7. **Extend general time limits** to 24 to 36 months.
8. **Make Bluefen consent, the Riverlark payout and discharge, and Mossvale/landlord confirmations conditions precedent**, or cover them with specific indemnities or price adjustments.
9. **Deduct the bonuses and any other debt-like items** from price, with the Seller bearing on-costs.
10. **Expand the Ironquay indemnity** beyond the SOW3 fee and require payment and a confirmatory assignment before Completion.
11. **Commission urgent privacy investigation** and a specific indemnity for the DD-006 incident. Establish the awareness date to check NDB timing.
12. **Require a bring-down disclosure** before Completion, with walk-away rights.
13. **Complete independent title verification.**

**Caveat:** Points on statutory timing (Privacy Act assessment periods, NSW limitation periods, payroll tax and superannuation treatment) should be confirmed by NSW counsel and tax advisers before we rely on them in negotiation.
